segment.description: Lake Barkley (Barkley Reservoir) Tennessee portion — the Cumberland River reservoir at the Kentucky line in Stewart and Montgomery counties (catalog); TWRA describes roughly 10,350 acres in Tennessee and 47,570 acres in Kentucky, managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, with an entirely warmwater sportfish list (largemouth/smallmouth/spotted bass, black/white crappie, bluegill/redear, white bass, catfish, sauger/walleye/saugeye, striped/hybrid bass, paddlefish). Trout are never mentioned on TWRA's page. Control-style water.
segment.boundaries: Tennessee portion of Barkley Reservoir along the Cumberland River (catalog counties Stewart and Montgomery), upstream of Barkley Dam which lies in Kentucky; TWRA references reaches 'between Cumberland City and the Kentucky state line'.

coldSource.notes: TWRA: the reservoir 'lies along the Cumberland River and is managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers'. It is a flood-control/navigation impoundment, not a cold tailwater; no cold-release regime is documented. Note the relevant geography: KDFWR documents that Cumberland River trout water runs from Wolf Creek Dam (Lake Cumberland, KY) only 'downstream to the Tennessee state line' — the managed trout reach ends at the state line and does not extend into this reservoir.

holdover.detail: No trout fishery of any kind is documented: TWRA's Barkley page lists no trout in its species, regulations, or fishing-tips content; the 2026 TWRA stocking schedule contains no Barkley entry (TWRA's page-note: Dale Hollow, not Barkley, is the regional trout reservoir); and the owner workbook has zero Barkley rows.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. TWRA's species documentation is entirely warmwater; the trout fishery on this section of the Cumberland system is Kentucky's Lake Cumberland tailwater above the state line, managed by KDFWR.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Warm USACE impoundment with an entirely warmwater documented fishery; the Cumberland's managed trout tailwater ends at the Tennessee state line above this reservoir, and no trout stocking program exists for Barkley on any source checked.
